Solution 1 gives n = 6 for q = 3, Solution 2 gives 5, and Solution 3 gives 5. All three exceed a code I checked directly.

For q = 3 and n = 4, take the three orthonormal symmetric states

- ψ₁ = (1/√3)|0000⟩ + √(2/3)|D₀₂₂⟩
- ψ₂ = (1/√3)|1111⟩ + √(2/3)|D₂₀₂⟩
- ψ₃ = (1/√3)|2222⟩ + √(2/3)|D₂₂₀⟩

Here |D_{abc}⟩ denotes the normalized Dicke state with the indicated occupation numbers of |0⟩, |1⟩, |2⟩. For example, |D₀₂₂⟩ is the uniform superposition over arrangements of {1,1,2,2}.

- **Orthogonality:** the three states have disjoint occupation-number supports.
- **Off-diagonal single-site errors:** |i⟩⟨j| with i≠j flips the parity of two occupation numbers, so its image is orthogonal to every codeword, which all have even occupations.
- **Diagonal single-site errors:** each codeword has ⟨n_i⟩ = 4/3 for every i, and cross terms between codewords vanish because the number operators are diagonal with disjoint supports. So every single-site operator compresses to a scalar on the code.

Hence distance at least 2 holds with dimension 3 at n = 4. This rules out all three formulas at q = 3, although I did not establish the exact minimum for q = 3 (it may be 3 or 4).

CHOICE: NONE
CONFIDENCE: 4
